items.description: A popular theme park in Buena Park, California. It began as a small berry farm and has grown into a major amusement park with roller coasters and other attractions.
facts: Located in Buena Park, California.
Started as a roadside berry stand.
America's first theme park.
Features a Ghost Town section.

items.description: A large desert and plateau region of the southwestern United States, covering the Four Corners area. It is known for its dramatic canyons and vibrant colors.
facts: Covers the Four Corners region.
Interspersed with dramatic canyons.
The Grand Canyon is located here.
Known for its high elevation and arid climate.

items.description: A major mountain range system of the North American Cordillera, that runs northwest–southeast through northwestern and western Mexico, and along the Gulf of California. A small portion extends into the US.
facts: Major mountain range in western Mexico.
Extends into Arizona and New Mexico.
Rich in mineral resources like silver.
Home to deep canyons, including Copper Canyon.

items.description: A mountain range located in the Big Bend National Park in Texas. It is the only mountain range in the United States to be fully contained within a single national park.
facts: Located in Big Bend National Park, Texas.
Fully contained within the national park.
Highest peak is Emory Peak.
Named for the Chisos Indigenous people.

items.description: A mountain range on the Olympic Peninsula in western Washington in the United States. The mountains are part of the Pacific Coast Ranges.
facts: Located on the Olympic Peninsula in Washington.
Highest peak is Mount Olympus.
Part of the Pacific Coast Ranges.
Features extensive glaciers.
